hook.line: At the café everyone has a view on Altamira, and sooner or later you want to say "it's obvious that..." and sound sure of yourself. Spanish has two ready-made openers for that.
hook.es: Está claro que Altamira quiere comprar la cuadra.
hook.en: It's clear that Altamira wants to buy the block.

examples.en: It's clear he made a mistake.

examples.es: Está claro que don Hernando tiene razón.
examples.en: It's clear that don Hernando is right.

examples.es: Es evidente que Simón tiene hambre.
examples.en: It's obvious that Simón is hungry.

examples.es: No está claro que Altamira compre el café.
examples.en: It isn't clear that Altamira will buy the café.

examples.es: No es evidente que Mariana tenga razón.
examples.en: It isn't obvious that Mariana is right.

rule:
Start with *está claro que* or *es evidente que* when you present something as a fact. What follows is an ordinary verb: *tiene*, *quiere*, *se equivocó*. English works the same way, so this part is easy.

The twist is the negative. *No está claro que* means you are not sure, so the verb after it switches to the wish form: *compre*, *tenga*.

Fact: *Está claro que tiene razón.*
Doubt: *No está claro que tenga razón.*

Keep *que* every time, and no *de* in front of it.
smallPrint: Teachers call these expressions of certainty. A fact takes the indicative; once you deny the certainty, the subjunctive takes over.

readAndPick.es: Está claro que Tomás tiene razón.
options: It isn't clear that Tomás is right.
It's clear that Tomás is right.

readAndPick.es: No está claro que Tomás tenga razón.
options: It's clear that Tomás is right.
It isn't clear that Tomás is right.

readAndPick.es: Es evidente que Simón tiene hambre.
options: It's obvious that Simón is hungry.
It isn't obvious that Simón is hungry.
Simón wasn't hungry.

readAndPick.es: No es evidente que Mariana tenga razón.
options: It's obvious that Mariana is right.
It isn't obvious that Mariana is right.

readAndPick.es: Está claro que Altamira quiere comprar la cuadra.
options: It's clear that Altamira wants to buy the block.
It isn't clear that Altamira wants to buy the block.
Altamira bought the block.

readAndPick.es: No está claro que Altamira compre el café.
options: It's clear that Altamira will buy the café.
It isn't clear that Altamira will buy the café.
It's clear that Altamira bought the café.
It isn't obvious that she's tired.
It's obvious that she's tired.

readAndPick.es: No está claro que Vale quiera irse.
options: It isn't clear that Vale wants to leave.
It's clear that Vale wants to leave.
Vale doesn't want to leave.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *tiene* or *tenga* and type the whole sentence: *Está claro que don Hernando ___ razón.*
yourTurn.answer: Está claro que don Hernando tiene razón.
yourTurn.why: You are stating a fact, so the verb stays ordinary: *tiene*.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *compra* or *compre* and type the whole sentence: *No está claro que Altamira ___ el café.*
yourTurn.answer: No está claro que Altamira compre el café.
yourTurn.why: Once it is *no está claro*, the verb takes the wish form: *compre*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: It's obvious that she's tired.
accept: Es evidente que ella está cansada.
yourTurn.why: *Es evidente que* plus an ordinary verb, because it is a fact.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: It's clear that Altamira wants to buy the block.
yourTurn.answer: Está claro que Altamira quiere comprar la cuadra.
yourTurn.why: A fact, so *quiere* stays as it is.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it negative: *Es evidente que Mariana tiene razón.* Say: It isn't obvious that Mariana is right.
yourTurn.answer: No es evidente que Mariana tenga razón.
yourTurn.why: Put *no* in front, and the verb switches to the wish form: *tenga*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: It isn't clear that Tomás will sell the café.
yourTurn.answer: No está claro que Tomás venda el café.
yourTurn.why: Not clear means not sure, so *venda*, not *vende*.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it a fact: *No está claro que Vale quiera irse.* Say: It's clear that Vale wants to leave.
yourTurn.answer: Está claro que Vale quiere irse.
yourTurn.why: Drop the *no* and the verb goes back to ordinary: *quiere*.

pitfalls.wrong: Está claro que Tomás tenga razón.
pitfalls.right: Está claro que Tomás tiene razón.
pitfalls.why: Almost. A fact takes the ordinary verb; the wish form is for when you are not sure.

pitfalls.wrong: No está claro que Altamira compra el café.
pitfalls.right: No está claro que Altamira compre el café.
pitfalls.why: Almost. After *no está claro que* you are doubting, so the verb takes the wish form.

pitfalls.wrong: Está claro de que Tomás tiene razón.
pitfalls.right: Está claro que Tomás tiene razón.
pitfalls.why: Almost. Nothing goes between *claro* and *que*: no *de*.

personal: Think of something that is obvious to you about your own town or job. Say it with *Está claro que* or *Es evidente que*.
